newsitem.title: JAPAN: Gajoen says seeks court mediation with creditors.
newsitem.headline: Gajoen says seeks court mediation with creditors.

text.p: Japanese hotel operator Gajoen Kanko KK announced late on Tuesday that it had decided to apply for court mediation with its creditors over its liabilities.

"We decided to apply for court mediation with our creditors... and even if we lack the qualifications for listing, we would like to continue operating as Gajoen Kanko KK," the company said in a statement.
Japanese banks suspended their transactions with Gajoen, retroactive to January 6, after it failed to honour promissory notes for a second time in December.
The Tokyo Stock Exchange announced on Wednesday that the firm's shares would be delisted from its first section on May 5.
Trading of the shares was suspended for Tuesday afternoon after a leading credit research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd reported that the company had become insolvent with debts of 9.88 billion yen.
